newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wall St weighs on Australian stocks at open.
newsitem.headline: Wall St weighs on Australian stocks at open.

text.p: The Australian share market opened lower on Thursday, weighed down by a Wall Street weakened by interest rate fears.
The gold sector resumed its downward trend as the bullion price dipped again in overseas markets.
From opening, the All Ordinaries index lost 8.5 points to 2,406.5.
"It looks like a general sentiment-driven market with the U.S. dictating the movements," said a dealer at a Melbourne-based brokerage.
Early attention was focussed on miners CRA and Pasminco with Pasminco saying it would buy CRA's controversial Century Zinc mine project in North Queensland for A$345 million.
CRA shares firmed three cents to A$19.58 (US$15.29) while Pasminco scrip slipped five cents to A$1.93 with unresolved issues such as native title creating concerns among players.
"It looks interesting. It is a pretty big investment and it is no sure deal to go through with native title issues," the dealer said.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about nine to four, while about 36 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
